to.name: Shadow: Google may reduce Broadcom custom TPU/ASIC orders
to.statement: Unconfirmed report (The Information, 2026-09-11, anonymous sources, source_tier 3, unknown source relationship) that Google may reduce Broadcom custom ASIC/TPU orders as it expands in-house silicon. Neither Google nor Broadcom has confirmed; no order volumes, revenue exposure, or timeline are disclosed. The report postdates Q3 FY2026 earnings (2026-09-02), so reported results contain no signal on it. If confirmed, it would be direct negative evidence on the hyperscaler customer concentration driver — in-house silicon substitution by a major AI customer, the exact loss-of-buyer mechanism the Brain already flags as the key risk to the guided AI ramp.
promotion_criteria: Public confirmation from Google or Broadcom (statement, earnings commentary, or filing)
Corroboration by an independent higher-tier source with named sourcing or data
Order, allocation, or supply-chain data confirming reduced Google TPU volumes at Broadcom
Quantification of Google's share of AVGO AI semiconductor revenue

proposals.reason: A rumor cannot advance to claims without verification and exposure sizing; this question defines the evidence required before any Base Case or Core Claim impact could even be considered.

to.question: What share of Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue (and total revenue) is attributable to Google custom TPU/ASIC orders, and is there any confirmation, denial, or corroborating order/supply-chain evidence for the reported reduction?
to.why_it_matters: The rumor's materiality cannot be sized without the exposure number. Current evidence attributes the guided AI ramp (doubling AI semiconductor revenue in each of the next two years) to Anthropic and OpenAI; Google's role and customer-level revenue are undisclosed. Verification status also gates whether the shadow state can ever be promoted toward the concentration claim.
